description: Mini-catchment weir records from an impact study of drain cleaning on water flows (Coalburn, Scotland) is a dataset listed in UK national open data portal, an open data portal, published or maintained by Forestry Commission. Coalburn in the north of England is Britain's longest running forest hydrology research catchment, providing a unique record of the long-term effects of conifer afforestation on upland water supplies since 1972. Coverage: United Kingdom. The portal files it under the publisher Forestry Commission. Its tags are Scotland, drainage, environment, hydrology, research. It offers 1 resource(s) in XLSX. The portal shows 2025-07-25 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the portal listing (dataset page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support flood defence and reservoir studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ckan-uk-portal.
